open_findings.title: The permission surface now ships, but a browser-side check is still not an authentication
open_findings.finding: REVISED 2026-09-22. The permission table, canRead, canAttach, makeDevIdentity and requireApprovedIdentity are now in the SHIPPED src/data/export.js, ported there so the case store's attachment check works in a browser. So the component-level permission logic is closed, and a participant cannot read the internal record through this component. What remains is narrower: there is no approved identity provider on this machine, so requireApprovedIdentity REFUSES an authenticated identity rather than accepting one. That refusal is deliberate - accepting one would be inventing authority - and a development identity is a declared role, not an authentication.
open_findings.impact: F08's disclosure half and its component-level access logic are both closed and tested. Real tenant policy, revocation and server-side enforcement remain unimplemented, because no backend exists here to provide them. A browser-side allowlist is not access control, and it is not described as one anywhere in the code.
open_findings.handling: Needs infrastructure and an identity owner. Until one exists, the honest position is the one the code takes: refuse an authenticated identity rather than invent authority.

open_findings.title: The candidate records carry no reporting period, and the source cannot supply one
open_findings.finding: ACCEPT-01 R27 fails and should stay failing. The 10543 candidate rows have no period, year or date field, though the screening rule is described as running on 2025/2024 and H1 2026/2025. Two rows also carry a null cost reconciliation because the price-file FOB value is empty - a null difference is not a match.
open_findings.handling: Needs a commercial or source input. Guessing the period is the one thing the brief forbids.

open_findings.title: The payload contains no comparable price observation that can be used
open_findings.finding: Every offer is excluded, dominated by PRODUCT_MATCH_UNRESOLVED (offers rest on seller cross-references, which is a candidate to inspect rather than approved equivalence) and PACK_CONTENTS_UNKNOWN (no offer declares whether its quote is for a piece or a pack). The panel is correct to exclude them all.
open_findings.impact: MARKET-07 has tested logic and a working screen but no answer. The commercial question - how our net terms compare with a competitor - cannot be answered from the data currently held.
open_findings.handling: Needs pack contents and an exact match basis in the source. No code change supplies either.

open_findings.title: The payload has no recorded digest, so an added key cannot be verified against the file's own statement
open_findings.finding: A key was added by hand to meta (marketComparisonDeclarations) because writing it back programmatically rewrote the envelope's recorded digest, which then no longer matched the file. The payload is excluded from version control, so it exists only on this machine with no history. The added key was verified against the authorised sibling copy instead: cases, candidateScreen, verifiedCosts, offers, sources and alternatives are all byte-identical, and exactly one key was added.
open_findings.impact: A restricted file that a reviewer cannot verify against its own recorded digest is weaker evidence than one that never carried the extra key. The byte difference is also explained: the repo copy is pretty-printed while the sibling is minified, which accounts for 1054709 of the 1054709 byte gap; the real content change is 2965 characters.
open_findings.handling: The right fix is a small builder in 01_data/91_build/ that regenerates the payload with its digest intact. That is outside the agent-owned area and is a decision about how the file should be produced.

open_findings.title: My own module_audit still over-reports, and the generated audits are stale
open_findings.finding: tools/module_audit.py is a raw text scan and cannot tell a deliberately declared comparison against a retired module from a misdirected load. It reports 11 retired loads where the guard says the genuinely misdirected count is 0. It now says so in its own output and names guard_09_module_scope.cjs as the authority. docs/ORPHAN_AUDIT.md and MODULE_AUDIT.md were also stale at commit time because the module lists changed after they were generated.
open_findings.handling: Either rework the tool to read the in-file declarations the way the guard does, or delete it and let the guard be the only answer. Regenerate both reports before any further commit.

open_findings.title: The payload still declares a split cost basis across alternatives
open_findings.finding: The ranking resolves every row to one offer date and reports a single baseline, so the screen no longer shows two baselines. The underlying payload still declares the split: the no-action rows for pads, cabin filter and oil filter use SEP26 while some alternatives use OCT26.
open_findings.handling: Data work, not a code fix.

open_findings.title: The oil migration cannot be calculated from the payload as supplied
open_findings.finding: Both product lines' parts costs are present and the Genuine line's list price appears in the option's prose, but no transferred quantity is stated anywhere and there is no applicable net selling price for the Genuine counterpart part number. The result is correctly unresolved rather than a fabricated zero.
open_findings.handling: Needs a stated transferred quantity and an applicable net selling price for the Genuine number.

open_findings.title: A country name appears where a distributor name is expected in the candidate rows
open_findings.finding: Candidate rows carry distributor labels ITUK and PORTUGAL. PORTUGAL is a country and the source never states which legal entity it is. ITUK and IUK are separate entities, and UTI and UMI must never be blended.
open_findings.handling: Not renamed - renaming would invent the entity. Kept visible with every label as it appears.

open_findings.title: One case's costRecordPresent flag contradicts verifiedCosts
open_findings.finding: One case carries a verified parts cost on the forward basis in verifiedCosts while its own packEvidence.costRecordPresent flag says false. The cost value is not repeated here: it is the restricted figure the payload holds, and it is cited by field name only. Checked all five cases: the flag agrees on four and disagrees on exactly one. So the objectives tab can rank a gross-profit alternative while the economics tab says no cost is applied.
open_findings.handling: Both statements are individually defensible; together they would confuse a reader. Needs a decision on which is authoritative for this case.

open_findings.title: The counts were taken against the payload staged before it was renewed, and cannot be re-derived without the restricted file
open_findings.finding: The restricted payload was regenerated during the session, so its bytes changed. Every count in _acceptance_run, and the artifact hash beside them, were taken against the payload staged before that renewal. The artifact itself was rebuilt AFTER the renewal and reproduces byte for byte, so the build is current; it is the counts that have not been re-derived against the renewed file.
open_findings.impact: Nothing is known to be wrong. The counts have not been re-derived against the renewed file, and doing so is a rebuild plus a full suite run. It cannot be finished from a clone: the payload is excluded from version control, so a machine without it cannot run these checks at all.
open_findings.handling: Re-run tests/run_all.ps1 against the renewed payload before treating these counts as current for that file.

open_findings.title: Restricted figures and part numbers had been copied into tracked files, and the sweep that finds them was blind to a part number on its own
open_findings.finding: A sweep reads the real cost figures and part numbers out of the restricted payload and searches every git-tracked file for them. Its first run found a four-decimal supplier cost beside a part number in the progress record and real payload data copied into the data-contract test fixture. Checking the work by hand found more than the sweep reported: the sweep matched a FOUR-DECIMAL figure, so a real part number on its own line, a named seller beside an advertised price, and costs quoted to two decimals all passed it. Restricted part numbers were found in nine tracked files, and named competitor prices and seller names in one.
open_findings.impact: The exclusion scheme keeps the payload, the frozen reference and the assembled HTML out of version control. It does not stop a restricted VALUE being quoted in a tracked document, and a tracked document is versioned forever. Nothing had been committed, so nothing needed a history rewrite. The fixture's own values were replaced with invented ones, the affected documents were rewritten to cite FIELD NAMES instead of figures, and the checks that read the real payload now derive what they need from it in memory rather than asserting a literal copied out of it.
open_findings.handling: The sweep's match rule should be widened: a restricted PART NUMBER is identifying on its own, and so is a cost quoted to two decimals in a cost context. Until it is widened, a clean sweep run is not evidence that no restricted value is quoted - it is evidence that none of the forms the sweep knows about is quoted.
